sanskrit: evam uktas tu pārthena śikhaṇḍī bharatarṣabha śarair nānāvidhais tūrṇaṃ pitāmaham upādravat
english: Thus addressed by Pārtha, O bull of the Bhāratas, Śikhaṇḍin swiftly rushed upon the grandsire with arrows of every kind.

sanskrit: acintayitvā tān bāṇān pitā devavratas tava arjunaṃ samare kruddhaṃ vārayām āsa sāyakaiḥ
english: Heedless of those shafts, your father Devavrata held off the wrathful Arjuna in battle with his own arrows.

sanskrit: tathaiva ca camūṃ sarvāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathaḥ apraiṣīt samare tīkṣṇaiḥ paralokāya māriṣa
english: And so too, O honored one, that great chariot-warrior dispatched the whole host of the Pāṇḍavas to the other world with his keen shafts in battle.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavā rājan sainyena mahatā vṛtāḥ bhīṣmaṃ pracchādayām āsur meghā iva divākaram
english: Likewise, O king, the Pāṇḍavas, surrounded by their great army, veiled Bhīṣma as clouds veil the day-maker sun.

sanskrit: sa samantāt parivṛto bhārato bharatarṣabha nirdadāha raṇe śūrān vanaṃ vahnir iva jvalan
english: Hemmed in on every side, that scion of Bharata, O bull of the Bhāratas, burned down the heroes in battle as a blazing fire consumes a forest.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma tava putrasya pauruṣam ayodhayata yat pārthaṃ jugopa ca yatavratam
english: There we beheld the wondrous prowess of your son, who fought against Pārtha and guarded the firm-vowed one.

sanskrit: karmaṇā tena samare tava putrasya dhanvinaḥ duḥśāsanasya tutuṣuḥ sarve lokā mahātmanaḥ
english: By that deed of your bowman son Duḥśāsana in battle, all the worlds were well pleased with the great-souled one.

sanskrit: yad ekaḥ samare pārthān sānugān samayodhayat na cainaṃ pāṇḍavā yuddhe vāyarām āsur ulbaṇam
english: For alone he fought against the Pārthas and their followers, and even so the Pāṇḍavas could not check that fierce warrior in the fray.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanena samare rathino virathīkṛtāḥ sādinaś ca mahārāja dantinaś ca mahābalāḥ
english: By Duḥśāsana in battle chariot-warriors were stripped of their cars, O great king, as were riders and mighty elephant-borne men.

sanskrit: vinirbhinnāḥ śarais tīkṣṇair nipetur dharaṇītale śarāturās tathaivānye dantino vidrutā diśaḥ
english: Pierced through by his sharp shafts, they fell to the earth's surface, while other elephants, tormented by arrows, fled in all directions.

sanskrit: yathāgnir indhanaṃ prāpya jvaled dīptārcir ulbaṇaḥ tathā jajvāla putras te pāṇḍavān vai vinirdahan
english: As fire, finding fuel, blazes up with fierce and brilliant flame, so did your son blaze, consuming the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: taṃ bhāratamahāmātraṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathaḥ jetuṃ notsahate kaś cin nāpy udyātuṃ kathaṃ cana ṛte mahendratanayaṃ śvetāśvaṃ kṛṣṇasārathim
english: That great captain of the Bhāratas no mighty car-warrior of the Pāṇḍavas dared to vanquish, nor in any way to advance against him — save the son of great Indra, he of the white horses, whose charioteer was Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: sa hi taṃ samare rājan vijitya vijayo 'rjunaḥ bhīṣmam evābhidudrāva sarvasainyasya paśyataḥ
english: For having conquered him in battle, O king, the victorious Arjuna rushed straight at Bhīṣma in the sight of all the army.

sanskrit: vijitas tava putro 'pi bhīṣmabāhuvyapāśrayaḥ punaḥ punaḥ samāśvasya prāyudhyata raṇotkaṭaḥ arjunaṃ ca raṇe rājan yodhayan sa vyarājata
english: Though vanquished, your son, taking refuge in the strength of Bhīṣma's arm, again and again rallied and fought on, fierce in the battle; and warring against Arjuna in the fray, O king, he shone resplendent.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī tu raṇe rājan vivyādhaiva pitāmaham śarair aśanisaṃsparśais tathā sarpaviṣopamaiḥ
english: But Śikhaṇḍin in battle, O king, kept piercing the grandsire with arrows whose touch was as the thunderbolt's and like the venom of serpents.

sanskrit: na ca te 'sya rujaṃ cakruḥ pitus tava janeśvara smayamānaś ca gāṅgeyas tān bāṇāñ jagṛhe tadā
english: Yet these wrought no pain in your father, O lord of men, and the son of Gaṅgā, smiling, then received those shafts.

sanskrit: uṣṇārto hi naro yadvaj jaladhārāḥ pratīcchati tathā jagrāha gāṅgeyaḥ śaradhārāḥ śikhaṇḍinaḥ
english: As a man scorched by heat welcomes the streaming rain, so the son of Gaṅgā received the showers of Śikhaṇḍin's arrows.

sanskrit: taṃ kṣatriyā mahārāja dadṛśur ghoram āhave bhīṣmaṃ dahantaṃ sainyāni pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām
english: The warriors beheld him, O great king, terrible in the fray — Bhīṣma, burning down the armies of the great-souled Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīt tava sutaḥ sarvasainyāni māriṣa abhidravata saṃgrāme phalgunaṃ sarvato rathaiḥ
english: Then your son said to all the troops, O honored one: 'Rush upon Phalguna in the battle with your chariots from every side!'

sanskrit: bhīṣmo vaḥ samare sarvān palayiṣyati dharmavit te bhayaṃ sumahat tvaktvā pāṇḍavān pratiyudhyata
english: 'Bhīṣma, knower of the law, will guard you all in battle. Casting off your great fear, fight back against the Pāṇḍavas!'

sanskrit: eṣa tālena dīptena bhīṣmas tiṣṭhati pālayan sarveṣāṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ raṇe śarma ca varma ca
english: 'Yonder Bhīṣma stands with his blazing palmyra banner, protecting all the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra — in battle their shelter and their shield.'

sanskrit: tridaśāpi samudyuktā nālaṃ bhīṣmaṃ samāsitum kim u pārthā mahātmānaṃ martyabhūtās tathābalāḥ tasmād dravata he yodhāḥ phalgunaṃ prāpya saṃyuge
english: 'Even the thirty gods, fully arrayed, are not able to assail the great-souled Bhīṣma — how much less the Pārthas, who are but mortals and feeble! Therefore charge, O warriors, and close with Phalguna in the fight!'

sanskrit: aham adya raṇe yatto yodhayiṣyāmi phalgunam sahitaḥ sarvato yattair bhavadbhir vasudhādhipāḥ
english: 'I myself, intent in battle today, will fight against Phalguna, joined on all sides by your eager selves, O lords of the earth!'

sanskrit: tac chrutvā tu vaco rājaṃs tava putrasya dhanvinaḥ arjunaṃ prati saṃyattā balavanto mahārathāḥ
english: Hearing that speech, O king, of your bowman son, the mighty great chariot-warriors made ready against Arjuna.

sanskrit: te videhāḥ kaliṅgāś ca dāśerakagaṇaiḥ saha abhipetur niṣādāś ca sauvīrāś ca mahāraṇe
english: The Videhas and the Kaliṅgas, together with the bands of the Dāśerakas, and the Niṣādas and the Sauvīras, fell upon him in that great battle.

sanskrit: bāhlikā daradāś caiva prācyodīcyāś ca mālavāḥ abhīṣāhāḥ śūrasenāḥ śibayo 'tha vasātayaḥ
english: The Bāhlīkas and the Daradas, the easterners and northerners, the Mālavas, the Abhīṣāhas, the Śūrasenas, the Śibis, and the Vasātis.

sanskrit: śālvāśrayās trigartāś ca ambaṣṭhāḥ kekayaiḥ saha abhipetū raṇe pārthaṃ pataṃgā iva pāvakam
english: The Śālvas and their dependents, the Trigartas, the Ambaṣṭhas, together with the Kekayas — all rushed upon Pārtha in battle as moths upon a flame.

sanskrit: sa tān sarvān sahānīkān mahārāja mahārathān divyāny astrāṇi saṃcintya prasaṃdhāya dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Calling to mind his divine weapons and fitting them to his bow, Dhanaṃjaya faced all those mighty car-warriors with their hosts, O great king.

sanskrit: sa tair astrair mahāvegair dadāhāśu mahābalaḥ śarapratāpair bībhatsuḥ pataṃgān iva pāvakaḥ
english: With those weapons of mighty speed the great-strong Bībhatsu swiftly burned them up by the searing power of his shafts, as fire burns moths.

sanskrit: tasya bāṇasahasrāṇi sṛjato dṛḍhadhanvinaḥ dīpyamānam ivākāśe gāṇḍīvaṃ samadṛśyata
english: As that firm-bowed one loosed his thousands of arrows, the Gāṇḍīva was seen blazing as it were in the sky.

sanskrit: te śarārtā mahārāja viprakīrṇarathadhvajāḥ nābyavartanta rājānaḥ sahitā vānaradhvajam
english: Tormented by his arrows, O great king, their chariot-banners scattered, the kings together could not stand against him of the ape-bannered car.

sanskrit: sadhvajā rathinaḥ petur hayārohā hayaiḥ saha gajāḥ saha gajārohaiḥ kirīṭiśaratāḍitāḥ
english: Car-warriors with their banners fell, horsemen along with their horses, and elephants with their riders, struck by the shafts of the Diademed One.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunabhujotsṛṣṭair āvṛtāsīd vasuṃdharā vidravadbhiś ca bahudhā balai rājñāṃ samantataḥ
english: Then the earth lay covered with the arrows loosed from Arjuna's arms, and on every side by the routed forces of the kings fleeing many ways.

sanskrit: atha pārtho mahābāhur drāvayitvā varūthinīm duḥśāsanāya samare preṣayām āsa sāyakān
english: Then the mighty-armed Pārtha, having put the host to flight, sent forth his shafts in battle against Duḥśāsana.

sanskrit: te tu bhittvā tava sutaṃ duḥśāsanam ayomukhāḥ dharaṇīṃ viviśuḥ sarve valmīkam iva pannagāḥ hayāṃś cāsya tato jaghne sārathiṃ ca nyapātayat
english: Those iron-tipped shafts, piercing through your son Duḥśāsana, all entered the earth as serpents enter an anthill; and then he slew his horses and struck down his charioteer.

sanskrit: viviṃśatiṃ ca viṃśatyā virathaṃ kṛtavān prabho ājaghāna bhṛśaṃ caiva pañcabhir nataparvabhiḥ
english: And with twenty shafts, O lord, he stripped Viviṃśati of his chariot, and smote him sorely with five smooth-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: kṛpaṃ śalyaṃ vikarṇaṃ ca viddhvā bahubhir āyasaiḥ cakāra virathāṃś caiva kaunteyaḥ śvetavāhanaḥ
english: Piercing Kṛpa, Śalya, and Vikarṇa with many iron shafts, the son of Kuntī, he of the white steeds, deprived them too of their chariots.

sanskrit: evaṃ te virathāḥ pañca kṛpaḥ śalyaś ca māriṣa duḥśāsano vikarṇaś ca tathaiva ca viviṃśatiḥ saṃprādravanta samare nirjitāḥ savyasācinā
english: Thus those five — Kṛpa and Śalya, O honored one, Duḥśāsana and Vikarṇa, and likewise Viviṃśati — stripped of their chariots and vanquished by Savyasācin, fled away from the battle.

sanskrit: pūrvāhṇe tu tathā rājan parājitya mahārathān prajajvāla raṇe pārtho vidhūma iva pāvakaḥ
english: In the forenoon, O king, having thus defeated those great car-warriors, Pārtha blazed up in the battle like a smokeless fire.

sanskrit: tathaiva śaravarṣeṇa bhāskaro raśmivān iva anyān api mahārāja pātayām āsa pārthivān
english: And so too with his rain of arrows, like the radiant sun with his beams, he brought down still other kings, O great king.

sanskrit: parāṅmukhīkṛtya tadā śaravarṣair mahārathān prāvartayata saṃgrāme śoṇitodāṃ mahānadīm madhyena kurusainyānāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca bhārata
english: Having turned the great car-warriors to flight with his showers of arrows, he set flowing in the battle a mighty river whose waters were blood, midway between the armies of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: gajāś ca rathasaṃghāś ca bahudhā rathibhir hatāḥ rathāś ca nihatā nāgair nāgā hayapadātibhiḥ
english: Elephants and bands of chariots were in many ways slain by the car-warriors; chariots were destroyed by elephants, and elephants by horsemen and foot-soldiers.

sanskrit: antarā chidhyamānāni śarīrāṇi śirāṃsi ca nipetur dikṣu sarvāsu gajāśvarathayodhinām
english: The bodies and heads of the warriors mounted on elephants, horses, and chariots, cut asunder in the midst, fell down in all directions.

sanskrit: channam āyodhanaṃ reje kuṇḍalāṅgadadhāribhiḥ patitaiḥ pātyamānaiś ca rājaputrair mahārathaiḥ
english: The field of battle shone, strewn with princes, great car-warriors wearing earrings and armlets, the fallen and the falling alike.

sanskrit: rathaneminikṛttāś ca gajaiś caivāvapothitāḥ pādātāś cāpy adṛśyanta sāśvāḥ sahayasādinaḥ
english: Foot-soldiers were seen cut down by chariot-wheels and crushed by elephants, together with horses and the riders of horses.

sanskrit: gajāśvarathasaṃghāś ca paripetuḥ samantataḥ viśīrṇāś ca rathā bhūmau bhagnacakrayugadhvajāḥ
english: Hosts of elephants, horses, and chariots fell on every side, and chariots lay shattered on the ground, their wheels, yokes, and banners broken.

sanskrit: tad gajāśvarathaughānāṃ rudhireṇa samukṣitam channam āyodhanaṃ reje raktābhram iva śāradam
english: Sprinkled with the blood of those streams of elephants, horses, and chariots, the covered battlefield shone like a red autumnal cloud.

sanskrit: śvānaḥ kākāś ca gṛdhrāś ca vṛkā gomāyubhiḥ saha praṇedur bhakṣyam āsādya vikṛtāś ca mṛgadvijāḥ
english: Dogs, crows, and vultures, wolves together with jackals, and monstrous beasts and birds howled as they came upon their prey.

sanskrit: vavur bahuvidhāś caiva dikṣu sarvāsu mārutāḥ dṛśyamāneṣu rakṣaḥsu bhūteṣu vinadatsu ca
english: Winds of many kinds blew in all directions, while demons appeared to sight and spirits cried aloud.

sanskrit: kāñcanāni ca dāmāni patākāś ca mahādhanāḥ dhūmāyamānā dṛśyante sahasā māruteritāḥ
english: Golden garlands and costly banners, swept up suddenly by the wind, were seen smoking as they whirled.

sanskrit: śvetacchatrasahasrāṇi sadhvajāś ca mahārathāḥ vinikīrṇāḥ sma dṛśyante śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ sapatākāś ca mātaṅgā diśo jagmuḥ śarāturāḥ
english: Thousands of white umbrellas and great chariots with their banners were seen scattered by hundreds and by thousands; and elephants with their pennons, tormented by arrows, fled in every direction.

sanskrit: kṣatriyāś ca manuṣyendra gadāśaktidhanurdharāḥ samantato vyadṛśyanta patitā dharaṇītale
english: And warriors, O lord of men, bearing maces, lances, and bows, were seen on every side fallen upon the earth's surface.

sanskrit: tato bhīṣmo mahārāja divyam astram udīrayan abhyadhāvata kaunteyaṃ miṣatāṃ sarvadhanvinām
english: Then Bhīṣma, O great king, loosing a celestial weapon, charged upon the son of Kuntī before the eyes of all the bowmen.

sanskrit: taṃ śikhaṇḍī raṇe yattam abhyadhāvata daṃśitaḥ saṃjahāra tato bhīṣmas tad astraṃ pāvakopamam
english: Śikhaṇḍin, armored, rushed against him as he stood intent in battle; thereupon Bhīṣma withdrew that weapon, which was like fire itself.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu kaunteyaḥ śvetavāhanaḥ nijaghne tāvakaṃ sainyaṃ mohayitvā pitāmaham
english: At that very moment the son of Kuntī, he of the white steeds, having bewildered the grandsire, struck down your army.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evaṃ vyūḍheṣv anīkeṣu bhūyiṣṭham anuvartiṣu brahmalokaparāḥ sarve samapadyanta bhārata
english: Saṃjaya said: When the armies were thus arrayed and for the most part still standing fast, all the warriors became bent upon the world of Brahmā, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: na hy anīkam anīkena samasajjata saṃkule na rathā rathibhiḥ sārdhaṃ na padātāḥ padātibhiḥ
english: For in that press army no longer clashed with army, nor chariots with chariot-warriors, nor foot-soldiers with foot-soldiers.

sanskrit: aśvā nāśvair ayudhyanta na gajā gajayodhibhiḥ mahān vyatikaro raudraḥ senayoḥ samapadyata
english: Horses fought not with horses, nor elephants with elephant-warriors; a great and terrible confusion arose between the two armies.

sanskrit: naranāgaratheṣv evaṃ vyavakīrṇeṣu sarvaśaḥ kṣaye tasmin mahāraudre nirviśeṣam ajāyata
english: As men, elephants, and chariots were thus scattered everywhere, in that vast and dreadful carnage all distinction vanished.

sanskrit: tataḥ śalyaḥ kṛpaś caiva citrasenaś ca bhārata duḥśāsano vikarṇaś ca rathān āsthāya satvarāḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ raṇe śūrā dhvajinīṃ samakampayan
english: Then Śalya and Kṛpa, and Citrasena, O Bhārata, and Duḥśāsana and Vikarṇa, those heroes mounting their chariots in haste, made the host of the Pāṇḍavas tremble in battle.

sanskrit: sā vadhyamānā samare pāṇḍusenā mahātmabhiḥ trātāraṃ nādhyagacchad vai majjamāneva naur jale
english: That army of the Pāṇḍavas, slaughtered in battle by those great-souled ones, found no rescuer, like a ship foundering in the water.

sanskrit: yathā hi śaiśiraḥ kālo gavāṃ marmāṇi kṛntati tathā pāṇḍusutānāṃ vai bhīṣmo marmāṇy akṛntata
english: As the winter season cuts to the vitals of cattle, so did Bhīṣma cut into the vital parts of the sons of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: atīva tava sainyasya pārthena ca mahātmanā nagameghapratīkāśāḥ pātitā bahudhā gajāḥ
english: By your army and by the great-souled Pārtha alike, elephants resembling mountains and clouds were brought down in great numbers.

sanskrit: mṛdyamānāś ca dṛśyante pārthena narayūthapāḥ iṣubhis tāḍyamānāś ca nārācaiś ca sahasraśaḥ
english: Leaders of men were seen being crushed by Pārtha, struck by his arrows and by his iron shafts in their thousands.

sanskrit: petur ārtasvaraṃ kṛtvā tatra tatra mahāgajāḥ ābaddhābharaṇaiḥ kāyair nihatānāṃ mahātmanām
english: Here and there great elephants fell with a cry of anguish; and with the ornament-decked bodies of the slain great-souled ones,

sanskrit: channam āyodhanaṃ reje śirobhiś ca sakuṇḍalaiḥ tasminn atimahābhīme rājan vīravarakṣaye bhīṣme ca yudhi vikrānte pāṇḍave ca dhanaṃjaye
english: and with heads still bearing earrings, the battlefield shone strewn over, in that exceedingly fearful slaughter of the bravest of heroes, O king, while Bhīṣma showed his valor in the fight and so did the Pāṇḍava Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: te parākrāntam ālokya rājan yudhi pitāmaham na nyavartanta kauravyā brahmalokapuraskṛtāḥ
english: Beholding the grandsire surging forward in the battle, O king, the Kauravas did not turn back, having set the world of Brahmā before them.

sanskrit: icchanto nidhanaṃ yuddhe svargaṃ kṛtvā parāyaṇam pāṇḍavān abhyavartanta tasmin vīravarakṣaye
english: Desiring death in battle and making heaven their goal, they advanced against the Pāṇḍavas in that slaughter of the noblest heroes.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāpi mahārāja smaranto vividhān bahūn kleśān kṛtān saputreṇa tvayā pūrvaṃ narādhipa
english: The Pāṇḍavas too, O great king, remembering the many and varied wrongs once done to them by you and your sons, O lord of men,

sanskrit: bhayaṃ tyaktvā raṇe śūrā brahmalokapuraskṛtāḥ tāvakāṃs tava putrāṃś ca yodhayanti sma hṛṣṭavat
english: those heroes, casting off fear in battle and setting the world of Brahmā before them, fought joyfully against your men and your sons.

sanskrit: senāpatis tu samare prāha senāṃ mahārathaḥ abhidravata gāṅgeyaṃ somakāḥ sṛñjayaiḥ saha
english: Then the commander, that great car-warrior, said to the army in the battle: 'Charge upon the son of Gaṅgā, O Somakas, together with the Sṛñjayas!'

sanskrit: senāpativacaḥ śrutvā somakāḥ saha sṛñjayaiḥ abhyadravanta gāṅgeyaṃ śastravṛṣṭyā samantataḥ
english: Hearing the commander's word, the Somakas with the Sṛñjayas rushed upon the son of Gaṅgā with a rain of weapons from every side.

sanskrit: vadhyamānas tato rājan pitā śāṃtanavas tava amarṣavaśam āpanno yodhayām āsa sṛñjayān
english: Being assailed, O king, your father, the son of Śaṃtanu, falling under the sway of wrath, fought against the Sṛñjayas.

sanskrit: tasya kīrtimatas tāta purā rāmeṇa dhīmatā saṃpradattāstraśikṣā vai parānīkavināśinī
english: To that illustrious one, O dear son, the wise Rāma had of old imparted the training in arms that destroys the armies of foes.

sanskrit: sa tāṃ śikṣām adhiṣṭhāya kṛtvā parabalakṣayam ahany ahani pārthānāṃ vṛddhaḥ kurupitāmahaḥ bhīṣmo daśa sahasrāṇi jaghāna paravīrahā
english: Relying on that training and wreaking destruction on the enemy's host, day after day the aged grandsire of the Kurus, Bhīṣma, slayer of hostile heroes, slew ten thousand of the Pārthas.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu divase prāpte daśame bharatarṣabha bhīṣmeṇaikena matsyeṣu pāñcāleṣu ca saṃyuge gajāśvam amitaṃ hatvā hatāḥ sapta mahārathāḥ
english: But when that tenth day had come, O bull of the Bhāratas, by Bhīṣma alone, among the Matsyas and the Pāñcālas in the fray, after slaying countless elephants and horses, seven great car-warriors were slain.

sanskrit: hatvā pañca sahasrāṇi rathināṃ prapitāmahaḥ narāṇāṃ ca mahāyuddhe sahasrāṇi caturdaśa
english: The great-grandsire slew five thousand car-warriors, and fourteen thousand foot-soldiers in that great battle,

sanskrit: tathā dantisahasraṃ ca hayānām ayutaṃ punaḥ śikṣābalena nihataṃ pitrā tava viśāṃ pate
english: and a thousand elephants likewise, and again ten thousand horses, were slain by the might of your father's training, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvamahīpānāṃ kṣobhayitvā varūthinīm virāṭasya priyo bhrātā śatānīko nipātitaḥ
english: Then, having thrown into turmoil the host of all the kings, the beloved brother of Virāṭa, Śatānīka, was struck down.

sanskrit: śatānīkaṃ ca samare hatvā bhīṣmaḥ pratāpavān sahasrāṇi mahārāja rājñāṃ bhallair nyapātayat
english: And having slain Śatānīka in battle, the valiant Bhīṣma, O great king, struck down thousands of kings with his broad-headed shafts.
